title: FRESH AIR DISTRIBUTION - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: How does the aircraft's fresh air system utilize the inlet openings, outlet valves, and the heat duct door to manage airflow into the cockpit and cabin areas?
answer: Fresh air is distributed through ducts from two inlet openings, one in each wing leading edge, to air outlet valves located in the cockpit/cabin area at the wing roots by the upper corners of the windshield, in the side walls just aft of the instrument panel, and above the passenger seat. Air outlet valve removal/installation is typical at each location. A door assembly, located on the right side of the fuselage between the firewall and door post, also allows fresh air to be routed into the heat ducts. The door is operated by a control on the instrument panel labeled CABIN AIR.

title: FRESH AIR DISTRIBUTION - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: During normal maintenance, what is the proper method for securing ducts to the airframe components in the fresh air distribution system?
answer: The majority of the fresh air distribution system components are riveted to the airframe and do not require replacement during normal maintenance. Ducts are secured to these components using clamps. If ducts become damages or worn, they should be replaced. AlI UU I LE I VMLVr

title: FRESH AIR DISTRIBUTION - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the detailed procedures for removing and reinstalling the wing root air outlet valve and its associated components, including the steps for removing the retaining ring, upholstery panel or headliner, ducting hose clamp, and installing the valve and related parts?
answer:
CAUTION: Incorrect use of solvent cleaners during panel replacement may lead to scratching on the wing root. Only use protective materials and ensure that ambient temperature is met before proceeding.

Remove Air Outlet Valve . (1) Remove retaining ring from air outlet valve. (2)  Remove upholstery panel or headliner. Refer to chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices. (3) Remove clamp securing ducting hose to air outlet valve adapter. (4)  Remove air outlet valve and adapter.Install Wing Root Air Outlet Valve . (1) Install air outlet valve and valve adapter to ducting. Secure with clamp. (2) Install upholstery panel or headliner. Refer to Chapter 25, Interior Upholstery - Maintenance Practices. (3) Install retaining ring to air outlet valve.

title: FRESH AIR DISTRIBUTION - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the key steps involved in routing and securing the Cabin Air Control Cable during installation to ensure proper operation?
answer:
NOTE: This procedure applies specifically to aircraft models with engine nacelle configurations post-2015. For older models, refer to AMM revision 22B or later. Always verify tool availability before beginning.

Remove Cabin Air Control Cable . (1) Carefully straighten end of CABIN AIR control cable. (2) Loosen clamp bolt on control arm and withdraw cable from control arm. (3) Remove screws securing clamp. (4) Gain access to the backside of the CABIN AIR control cable. (5) Loosen nut on backside of control cable. (6) Carefully withdraw cable from instrument panel.Install Cabin Air Control Cable . (1) Thread end of control cable through hole in instrument panel. (2) Secure CABIN AIR control cable to backside of instrument panel using existing jamnut. (3) Thread end of control cable through the clamp bolt. (4)  Clamp control housing. (5) Test control cable to ensure full range of travel. Travel may be adjusted by positioning control housing in clamps. (6) When full range of travel has been established, bend end of control cable around clamp bolt.

question: What are the specific procedures for threading, securing, and testing the Cabin Air Control Cable during installation to ensure proper operation and full travel?
answer:
NOTE: This procedure applies specifically to aircraft models with engine nacelle configurations post-2015. For older models, refer to AMM revision 22B or later. Always verify tool availability before beginning.

Remove Cabin Air Control Cable . (1) Carefully straighten end of CABIN AIR control cable. (2) Loosen clamp bolt on control arm and withdraw cable from control arm. (3) Remove screws securing clamp. (4) Gain access to the backside of the CABIN AIR control cable. (5) Loosen nut on backside of control cable. (6) Carefully withdraw cable from instrument panel.Install Cabin Air Control Cable . (1) Thread end of control cable through hole in instrument panel. (2) Secure CABIN AIR control cable to backside of instrument panel using existing jamnut. (3) Thread end of control cable through the clamp bolt. (4)  Clamp control housing. (5) Test control cable to ensure full range of travel. Travel may be adjusted by positioning control housing in clamps. (6) When full range of travel has been established, bend end of control cable around clamp bolt.
